top_signals.title: BofA: Hormuz Needs 10 Times More Ships to Stabilize Oil Markets
top_signals.summary: Bank of America (BoFA) is warning that oil prices could continue climbing into the winter if the U.S. and Iran fail to reach an agreement reopening the Strait of Hormuz, with severe shortages already emerging in diesel, gasoline and global natural gas markets. “We’ve been expecting oil to be in the $70 to $80 a barrel range for Brent on the assumption that we were going to see some resolution,” Francisco Blanch, Bank of America’s head of commodities and derivatives research, told CNBC on Monday. “But if we don’t,…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: U.S. oil rises back above $81 as doubt grows Washington and Tehran will reach Hormuz deal
top_signals.summary: Oil rose as traders assess mixed signals from the U.S. and Iran amid worries that a deal to open the Strait of Hormuz may not come anytime soon.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: FreightWaves CEO Says Freight Recession Is Over
top_signals.summary: Craig Fuller, CEO of FreightWaves, sees stronger trucking, rail and container volumes. He tells Vonnie Quinn on Bloomberg Open Interest that higher freight rates should have only a marginal impact on consumer inflation. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Inflation expectations impacting rate path, bonds and global risk assets.
